description.narrative: The development objective of Second Kenya Urban Support Program (KUSP2) Project is to strengthen the capacities of urban institutions to: (i) improve the delivery and resilience of urban infrastructure and services; (ii) enhance the private sector engagement in urban planning; and (iii) support the transition of refugee camps into integrated host community and refugee settlements. KUSP2 will support reforms, interventions, and actions in five Results Areas (RAs): RA 1 - Strengthened institutions for urban service delivery; RA 2 - Integrated planning for inclusive31 and resilient urban areas; RA 3 - More inclusive and resilient urban services and infrastructure; RA 4 - Improved private sector engagement; and RA 5 - Improved integrated development for refugees and host communities. The program for results (PforR) program will support some elements of the government program.

condition.narrative: Schedule 1. Section I.1. (Grant E208-KE)For the purpose of carrying out the Operation in Participating Refugee Hosting Counties,the Recipient through SDHUD shall, by no later than three months after the Effective Date, enter into and thereafter maintainthroughout the period of implementation of the Operation, an output agreement with a UN Agency, in form and substance satisfactoryto the Association (“Output Agreement”), whereby the Recipient shall: (a) hire the services of the UN Agency to implement theOperation in Participating Refugee Hosting Urban Areas in accordance with the provisions of the Operations Manual, and therequirements of the ESCP; and (b) agree on the direct payment/advance of the proceeds of the Financing from the Association to theUN Agency.

Schedule 2. Section I.A.4.b. (Credit 7349-KE) Without limitation to Section I.A.4(a) above, the NPCT shall be chaired by a Programcoordinator; and no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, the Recipient shall recruit/second to the NPCT –andthereafter maintain throughout the implementation of the Operation – additional staff (apart from the Program coordinator,procurement specialist, an accountant, finance officer, an environmental specialist, and a social specialist, in place by theEffective Date) with terms of reference and resources satisfactory to the Association, including an environmental specialist, asocial specialist, a health and safety specialist, a DRS liaison, a CoG liaison, and such other staff as may be detailed in theOperations Manual.

Schedule 2. Section I.B.1 (Credit 7349-KE) Without limitation on the generality of Part A of this Section I, the Recipient shallenter into an Intergovernmental Agreement with a respective Participating County, in form and substance satisfactory to theAssociation, which shall provide details on the mutual responsibilities for the implementation of the Operation, including theobligation of the respective Participating County to: (i) establish a CPCT referred to in Section I.A.5 of Schedule 2 to thisAgreement; (ii) carry out its activities under the Operation with due diligence and efficiency and in accordance with theOperations Manual; (iii) maintain policies and procedures adequate to enable it to monitor the progress of its activities under theOperation and the achievement of the Operation's objectives; (iv) enable the Recipient and the Association to inspect the Operationactivities within the respective Participating County's jurisdiction, and any relevant records and documents; and (v) prepare andfurnish to the Recipient and the Association all such information as the Recipient or the Association may reasonably requestrelating to the foregoing

Schedule 2. Section I.D.1 (Credit 7349-KE) The Recipient shall maintain appropriate monitoring and evaluation arrangements for theProgram satisfactory to the Association, including DLIs verification protocols. To this end, except as the Association shallotherwise agree in writing, the Recipient shall:(a) engage not later than four (4) months after the Effective Date, and thereaftermaintain throughout the period of implementation of the Program, one or more verification agents with experience, independence, andcapacity and under the terms of reference acceptable to the Association (“Independent Verification Agent(s)”) to monitor, audit,analyze and/ or verify the data and other evidence supporting the achievement/ fulfilment of one or more Disbursement LinkedResults (“DLRs”) as set forth in Schedule 3 to this Agreement; (b) cause the Independent Verification Agent(s) to undertakeverification audit(s) in accordance with verification protocols agreed with the Association and detailed in the Operations Manual,and thereafter furnish to the Association the corresponding report(s) of the Independent Verification Agent(s) in a timely mannerand in form and substance satisfactory to the Association, as detailed in the verification protocols.

Schedule 2. Section V.1 (Credit 7349-KE) The Recipient shall, not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, establishan operational complaints handling and management system for the Operation, such system to include, a complaints/grievancecommittee to handle complaints, designated focal complaints officer to coordinate the system, an established feedback mechanism anda service charter prescribing how complaints related to the Operation will be handled.
